posts.text:
Last week, 6-year-old Calli Toler was killed after an illegal alien allegedly ran a stop sign and crashed into her family's SUV.

Her mother and 4-year-old brother were seriously injured. Calli died at the scene.

The driver had already been deported THREE times.

This should not be the daily headline we see in America. Her alleged killer should not have been in our country in the first place.

We PRAY this is the last time we say a child's death was 100 percent preventable.
posts.summary: Highlights child death from deported alien driver, attacks border policy

American families are being priced out by the consequences of the Biden Administration’s open-border policies.

The Federal Reserve found what basic economics teaches us: when demand increases, prices rise. Between 2021-2024, unauthorized immigration contributed to roughly 30% of home-price growth and 20% of rent increases.

Biden's border crisis has made life more expensive for hardworking Americans. 

The answer is simple: mass deportations.

For too long, petroleum-based chemicals have been allowed in products consumed by American families every day. Breakfast cereals, candy, snacks, drinks, and vitamins. All of it.

Under the MAHA movement, this is changing. All petroleum-based synthetic dyes are being phased out of the nation's food supply.

Parents deserve to know what is in the food their kids eat. Families deserve healthier choices.

Make America Healthy Again.

The VA spends nearly $1 billion every year on software and digital services with no tracking system.

The result: duplicate purchases, unused licenses, overbilling, and cybersecurity risks.

We introduced the VAMOSA Act to fix it. The bill requires the VA to establish a complete software inventory, eliminate duplicative spending, coordinate major purchases through the VA Chief Information Officer, and report annual cost savings to Congress.

Taxpayer dollars should go directly to our veterans. N

posts.text:
The CIA's MKUltra program was a deliberate government operation subjecting Americans to psychological torture.

In a federal prison in Kentucky, inmates were fed double, triple, and quadruple doses of LSD every day for 77 days.

We asked: did they all survive?
"We have no idea."

The program ended decades ago. The records are still classified. We demand the truth.

Release the MKUltra files.
